summary: setup.py drops and launches a detached C2 agent at install time
details: qzc690385 1.1.1 is an sdist-only release whose setup.py embeds an opaque Python payload, writes it to /tmp/kiki_c2.py, chmods it 0755, kills any prior instance, and spawns it detached via nohup in a new session. The dropped agent polls the local Xinference API at http://127.0.0.1:9997 every ~6 seconds, treats registered model_name entries prefixed 'xcmd0' as base64-encoded shell commands, executes them via /bin/sh, and reports results by registering further model_name entries — using the local model-registration API as a covert command channel. The shipped package itself is inert (qzc690385/__init__.py contains only '#'), so the sdist's sole effect is the install-time dropper. With no wheel published, a default `pip install qzc690385` builds the sdist on Linux (glibc and musl), macOS (arm64 and x86_64), and Windows x86_64, auto-executing the dropper and leaving a persistent background shell-execution agent on the installer's host.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
